title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LONNIE'S SUIT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lonnie Carver, a road crew flagger from Joplin, Missouri.
All day, he holds a sign that says SLOW. He says maybe ten words.
And one summer, he became a six-foot-four possum.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE OFFER
segments.quote: Life is like playing a violin solo in public and learning the instrument as one goes on.
segments.author: Samuel Butler
lines: The Joplin Possums, the town's summer ball team, lost their mascot right before opening day.
The suit only fit one man in town. Lonnie said, absolutely not.
That night his wife Rita read him a line from the English writer Samuel Butler:
Life is like playing a violin solo in public and learning the instrument as one goes on.
Lonnie sighed. Then he called the team. Fine. Yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: OPENING NIGHT
segments.quote: Angels can fly because they take themselves lightly.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: Opening night, ninety-four degrees. Inside the fur, it felt like two hundred.
He tripped on a bat bag and rolled down the dugout steps. Everybody laughed.
He wanted to hide. Then he remembered G. K. Chesterton:
Angels can fly because they take themselves lightly.
So Lonnie stood up and took a big, slow bow. The crowd went wild.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: ROW THREE
segments.quote: Love is the only force capable of transforming an enemy into a friend.
segments.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
lines: In row three sat Big Vern, who threw peanuts and yelled, Possums are rats!
Lonnie wanted to sit on him. Instead, he thought of Martin Luther King Junior:
Love is the only force capable of transforming an enemy into a friend.
So every game, Lonnie brought Vern a lemonade. No words.
By July, Vern was dancing with him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE GARAGE
segments.quote: Baseball is ninety percent mental. The other half is physical.
segments.author: Yogi Berra
lines: But by the seventh inning, Lonnie was always out of gas.
The team's old coach laughed and quoted Yogi Berra:
Baseball is ninety percent mental. The other half is physical.
So Lonnie worked on both. Morning walks. Dance moves in the garage.
His neighbors brought lawn chairs.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE HUG
segments.quote: Do not the most moving moments of our lives find us all without words?
segments.author: Marcel Marceau
lines: On the last night, his grown daughter Kim came. They hadn't talked much in years.
Lonnie never knew what to say.
Rita whispered words from Marcel Marceau, the famous French mime:
Do not the most moving moments of our lives find us all without words?
So the big possum just hugged her. Kim laughed, cried, and stayed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SIGN
segments.quote: Let us be thankful for the fools. But for them the rest of us could not succeed.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: Monday, Lonnie was back on the road with his SLOW sign.
A driver yelled, Hey, possum! You look like a fool!
Lonnie grinned, out of words for the day, and thought of Mark Twain:
Let us be thankful for the fools. But for them the rest of us could not succeed.
Then he danced with his sign. The whole line of cars honked.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say yes. Laugh at yourself. Bring the lemonade. Train. Hug. Be the fool.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes. Laugh at yourself. Bring the lemonade. Train. Hug more. Be the happy fool.
I tried a mascot suit once. They said I already had the belly.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
